cases.name: a vault at a revision JavaScript cannot count exactly
cases.why: JavaScript reads 9007199254740993 as 9007199254740992 and refuses a count it cannot hold exactly. Rust refuses what JavaScript would misread.

cases.name: a byte-order mark before the payload

cases.name: an epoch written 1.0
cases.why: JavaScript reads the number a JSON token stands for, so 1.0 and 1e0 are 1. Go and Rust read a count only from a whole number as written.

cases.name: a sequence number written -0
cases.why: JavaScript and Go read -0 as zero. serde_json reads it as a fraction, and a count is not read from one.

cases.name: an incoming-share key that is false
cases.why: JavaScript takes anything falsy for no key. Go and Rust take a string, null or nothing.

cases.name: a field's name in capitals
cases.why: Go matches a field's name without regard to case, the long s and the Kelvin sign included. JavaScript and Rust take the exact name, and Rust refuses a payload Go would read differently.

cases.name: a device name given twice, the second time capitalized
cases.why: JavaScript reads the device as Laptop and Go as Other: the same signed bytes, two states. Rust refuses them.

cases.name: a field written twice, where the last one counts
cases.why: JavaScript and Go take the last of two. Rust refuses a payload that says a thing twice, because the two do not always agree on which one counts.

cases.name: a field written twice, the same both times

cases.why: Go leaves a field as it was when it meets null, so it keeps the value before; JavaScript takes the null. The same signed bytes, two states. Rust refuses them.

cases.name: a byte that is not UTF-8 in a device name
cases.why: Go reads the byte as U+FFFD. The viewer and Rust refuse text that is not UTF-8.

cases.name: half of a surrogate pair escaped in a device name
cases.why: A name holds whole characters. Go reads the half as U+FFFD and would write the device back under that name; the viewer and the service refuse the name, and serde_json refuses the escape.

cases.name: half of a surrogate pair escaped in an unknown field
cases.why: JavaScript keeps the half and Go reads it as U+FFFD. serde_json refuses the escape, and with it the payload.

cases.name: an unknown field nested 200 deep
cases.why: serde_json stops at 128 levels, as it does for a session document.

cases.name: an event longer than the hosted service stores
cases.why: The service refuses an event of more than 32 KiB as text, and Rust keeps to that limit before decoding anything. Go and the viewer have no limit of their own.
